sourceSystem.description: Indicates the source system from which this canonical is imported

timestamp.description: Indicates the timestamp of the canonical in source system

sourcesId.description: Id of the {@link Sources} for the Source

orderCreationDatetime.description: The date order was created on the source system.

supplier.description: The {@link Supplier} from which this order is being shipped.

orderType.description: The type of order can be one of: Purchase or Transfer.

orderCanceled.description:
Flag to indicate whether this {@link PurchaseOrder} has been canceled.

If this purchase order has child {@link PurchaseOrderLine}s, the `orderCanceled` also
needs to be set to true. See field documentation on `orderCanceled` on how to handle
scenarios where the order canceled flag is not provided as part of the file export.

orderCanceledDatetime.description:
The datetime when this {@link PurchaseOrder} was canceled. This field must be populated if {@link #orderCanceled}
is set to true.

orderLines.description: The {@link PurchaseOrderLine} array for the {@link PurchaseOrder}

title:
The base canonical for {@link PurchaseOrder}.

The {@link PurchaseOrder} Type mixes in `SourceSystemAware`, but the base transform
does not add `sourceGroupId` to the order IDs. This is because orders are generally a number that is incremented
with each new order. Even if all other entity `id` conflicts are intentional across two ERPs, it is unlikely
that order `id` conflicts are intentional. If this is true for your customer, please concatenate the
`sourceGroupId` to the order `id` before passing it into the base canonicals/transforms.
name: CanonicalPurchaseOrder
